raw_response:
I'm 64 years old and I've farmed these fields in Quzhou County my whole life. I only finished primary school, so I don't read farming manuals — I watch what my neighbors do and remember what worked in years past. My family has 7 mu of land. This year I'll plant 5 mu with winter wheat in early October, using the improved *shimai* variety that Old Wang down the road swears by. After we cut the wheat in early June, I'll plant summer maize right away with no time for ploughing — we always direct-seed into the wheat stubble now. The other 2 mu I'll keep for cotton, which we plant in April and pick through autumn. Cotton brings good money but needs a lot of spraying. For fertilizer, I learned long ago that it's better to use a little too much than too little and risk a bad harvest. For the wheat I'll put down about 22 kg of nitrogen per mu, along with some phosphorus and potassium. I buy compound fertilizer from the co-op — roughly two bags for the wheat plot. The maize gets a bit less, around 20 kg nitrogen per mu, and the cotton about 14 kg. I'll irrigate the wheat three times: at green-up, jointing, and filling. The maize gets two waters if the rain doesn't come. For pesticides, wheat and maize are easy — three sprays each, mostly herbicide and some insecticide. But cotton is trouble — I'll spray about ten times to keep the bollworms off. I expect the wheat to give me about 450 kg per mu, the maize about 520 kg per mu, and the cotton around 260 kg per mu if the weather holds.
